claim: AI governance in industrial marketing fails because teams treat it as an IT security audit instead of a brand compliance protocol.
hook: AI governance is failing your marketing team.

evidence.detail: Observed review cycles where enterprise IT cleared AI tools for data security, but left zero protocols for technical accuracy, regulatory claims, or specification drift in heavy industry collateral.

slides.headline: AI governance is failing your marketing team.
IT security clears the tool, not the output
slides.body: Data security approval does not verify generated product claims. Assign an owner for technical accuracy.

slides.headline: Two checks before any AI copy goes live
slides.body: Check technical claims against approved documents, then check tone. Record who approved the final draft.

slides.headline: Governance is a queueing problem
slides.body: Match publication volume to the time available for technical review. Keep unverified drafts out of the release queue.

items.label: Review Capacity
items.detail: Limited hours of senior technical oversight

slides.headline: AI governance is a verification pipeline
slides.body: Treat generated copy as a draft. Give reviewers enough time to verify it before publication.

items.label: Action
items.detail: Send this to whoever reviews AI copy today

caption:
AI governance is failing your marketing team.

AI governance for marketing teams needs an owner for technical accuracy.

Most enterprises treat AI risk as an IT issue. They worry about data privacy while their teams use marketing automation to generate unverified technical specifications for heavy machinery.

When a consumer brand hallucinates a feature, customer support handles it. When an industrial brand hallucinates a load rating, a procurement committee walks away permanently.

Set the boundary rules before you scale the output.

Send this to whoever is defending AI content standards this quarter.
